old: One meaning traces back to a Latin word for 'head' — the same root hiding inside 'chief' and 'captain.'
A rocky point jutting into the sea once shared this very name, borrowed through Old French from that Latin word for head.
The other sense comes through Old Occitan and Late Latin 'cappa' — think of the cloth draped over a superhero's shoulders.
clues: This garment has a spelling twin naming a point of land, which traces back to an ancient root meaning "head," the same root behind chief and chef.
A sleeveless outer garment fastened at the neck and hanging loose over the shoulders and back, usually shorter than a cloak; Superman and Batman famously wear one.
On a map it means a headland jutting into the sea, as in ___ Cod or ___ Town, and slang uses it as a verb for defending someone.
